title: Pager truncate-image state

scope.rationale: sqlite3PagerTruncateImage records a smaller logical database size immediately before commit without touching the file. Commit phase one later applies that size physically, while rollback restores the transaction's original size.
excluded_responsibilities: B-tree determination of the target page count
Commit-phase physical file truncation and sync
Savepoint rollback after a final truncate-image request

external_source_responsibilities: Caller invokes this only immediately before commit from a modified write transaction
dependencies.caller_closure: The complete state mutation and both source precondition assertions are assigned. Production commit phase one multiplies database_pages by page_size and truncates the file; rollback restores original_database_pages.

inputs: Writable Pager in writer-cache-modified or writer-database-modified state and a page count no greater than the current logical image
contracts.ownership: Scalar Pager transaction state only; cached pages and file storage retain their existing owners.
contracts.state_and_results: Valid calls replace database_pages exactly without truncating cache or file. Read-only, growth, or invalid-state requests are rejected by the Zig API instead of relying only on source assertions.
contracts.locks_callbacks_io: Caller owns Pager synchronization. No callback or I/O occurs in this function.
contracts.failure_and_continuation: A rejected request preserves state. After success the transaction must commit or roll back; commit applies the size and rollback restores the original.

representation_differences: The C function is void and enforces preconditions with assertions. Zig returns READONLY or MISUSE for invalid public/internal calls while performing the same scalar mutation on valid input.
Neither implementation truncates the cache at this boundary; obsolete pages remain available for rollback and are reconciled by commit/rollback owners.

oracle.protocol: Open a writable Pager, begin and modify a transaction, reject growth, record a smaller image, observe unchanged file size before commit, then separately commit and roll back to compare physical and logical continuation.
internal_observations: logical page count before and after request
oracle.normalization: Page counts, file sizes, states, and result codes compare exactly.

assurance.io_crash_concurrency: No direct I/O. Existing commit crash ordering owns the later truncate/sync boundary; caller owns Pager synchronization.
assurance.malformed_input: Growth and invalid transaction states are rejected without mutation.
assurance.continuation: Rollback restores original_database_pages; commit phase one applies the selected size before sync.

integration.production_owner: src/core/pager.zig Pager transaction, commit, rollback, and file-size state
integration.native_call_path: B-tree/backup final-size owner -> Pager.truncateImage -> database_pages -> commitPhaseOne truncateFile, or rollback original_database_pages restoration.
integration.bounded_owner_retired: The production Pager no longer returns a read-only placeholder for writable truncate-image requests.

independent_review.notes: Requires B-tree/backup caller integration, scoped commit/rollback receipt, and independent review.

known_blockers: Route production B-tree and backup final-size operations through Pager.truncateImage.
Capture a scoped durable commit/rollback/crash receipt before internal-trace promotion.
